doc: Specs for the new lesson lines the staged plan proposes. The free drafter writes the line; verify-skill-curricula.js checks it with the subject's own validate.js rules, and two free judges review it.

specs.subject: piano
specs.insert_after: Shape One Practice Session From Warm-Up to Review
specs.learner: Elementary 2 (about ABRSM Grade 2), child or adult, already plays C, G, D, F and A major scales
specs.teach: Once each short unit (a scale, a chord change, a 2-bar figure) has been played correctly once, practise the units in a shuffled order instead of repeating one many times; it feels worse during practice but the next day's cold take is better, and our own sense of how well we learned points the wrong way, so check the next-day cold-take log.
facts: Random-order practice of short melodies was retained better two days later than fixed-order practice, while learners judged the opposite (Abushanab and Bishara 2013).
Shuffle only after each unit has had one correct run; do not shuffle long pieces.
specs.example: the G, D, F and A major scales in a shuffled order
avoid: Practise in Small Chunks Then Link Them
Interleaving and Spacing Pieces Across the Week
Major Key Tour: Scales, Triads and Cadences

specs.subject: basketball
specs.insert_after: Box Score and Shooting Percentages From Your Games
specs.learner: Ages 10-12, first 5v5 club player who just learned to compute shooting percentage
specs.teach: Ten shots tell you very little: 7 of 10 and 5 of 10 cannot be told apart reliably, so log at least fifty attempts over several days before deciding whether a change to your shot worked.
facts: With 10 attempts the 95% range around 7 of 10 runs from about 40% to about 89%, and around 5 of 10 from about 24% to about 76%, so the ranges overlap.
At 50 attempts the 95% margin for a 70% shooter is about 13 percentage points either way.
specs.example: 7 of 10 on Monday and 5 of 10 on Tuesday from the same spot
avoid: Box Score and Shooting Percentages From Your Games

specs.subject: basketball
specs.insert_after: Short Daily Sessions Beat One Long Cram
specs.learner: Ages 12-14 club or middle-school player, full-size ring
specs.teach: Judge what you learned by your first set of the next day from that spot, taken after the general warm-up but before shooting that spot again, because repeating one shot many times in a row makes today's percentage look better than what you will keep.
facts: In motor-learning studies, blocked (same-shot) practice gives the best scores during practice but varied or random practice gives better retention and transfer (contextual interference; in novices' jump shots blocked practice was most accurate during practice, Shamshiri et al. 2025).
Log the first ten shots from the spot the next day as the cold score.
specs.example: ten elbow jump shots the next day before any other shooting from the elbow
avoid: Short Daily Sessions Beat One Long Cram
Deliberate Practice: One Focus, Then Game-Speed Reps
